<bpmn:definitions xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL" id="Definitions_ClaimReview" targetNamespace="http://example.org/bpmn/claim-review">
  <bpmn:process id="Process_ClaimReview" name="Claim Review" isExecutable="false">
    <bpmn:laneSet id="LaneSet_ClaimReview">
      <bpmn:lane id="Lane_ClaimsOfficer" name="Claims Officer">
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>StartEvent_ClaimRegistered</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_ExamineClaim</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_WriteRecommendation</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
      </bpmn:lane>
      <bpmn:lane id="Lane_SeniorClaimsOfficer" name="Senior Claims Officer">
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_CheckRecommendation</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Gateway_ClaimOK</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>EndEvent_ProceedClaimHandling</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
      </bpmn:lane>
    </bpmn:laneSet>

    <bpmn:startEvent id="StartEvent_ClaimRegistered" name="Claim registered">
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_RegisteredToExamine</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:startEvent>

    <bpmn:userTask id="Task_ExamineClaim" name="Examine claim">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_RegisteredToExamine</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_ExamineToWrite</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:userTask>

    <bpmn:userTask id="Task_WriteRecommendation" name="Write settlement recommendation">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_ExamineToWrite</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_NotOKToWrite</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_WriteToCheck</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:userTask>

    <bpmn:userTask id="Task_CheckRecommendation" name="Check settlement recommendation">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_WriteToCheck</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_CheckToGateway</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:userTask>

    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_ClaimOK" name="Claim marked OK?">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_CheckToGateway</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_OKToProceed</bpmn:outgoing>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_NotOKToWrite</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:exclusiveGateway>

    <bpmn:endEvent id="EndEvent_ProceedClaimHandling" name="Proceed with claim handling">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_OKToProceed</bpmn:incoming>
    </bpmn:endEvent>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_RegisteredToExamine" sourceRef="StartEvent_ClaimRegistered" targetRef="Task_ExamineClaim"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_ExamineToWrite" sourceRef="Task_ExamineClaim" targetRef="Task_WriteRecommendation"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_WriteToCheck" sourceRef="Task_WriteRecommendation" targetRef="Task_CheckRecommendation"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_CheckToGateway" sourceRef="Task_CheckRecommendation" targetRef="Gateway_ClaimOK"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_OKToProceed" name="OK" sourceRef="Gateway_ClaimOK" targetRef="EndEvent_ProceedClaimHandling"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_NotOKToWrite" name="Not OK" sourceRef="Gateway_ClaimOK" targetRef="Task_WriteRecommendation"/>
  </bpmn:process>
</bpmn:definitions>

rules.instruction: When the description states that one participant reviews an item produced by another participant, and that the same participant then records an outcome on it (such as OK or Not OK) that decides the next step, with the review and the recording of the outcome described as separate actions: Model the review and the recording of the outcome as separate tasks: first a task for the review, then a task for recording the outcome, both before the exclusive gateway that routes on that outcome. Do not merge the review and the outcome recording into one task, and do not connect the decision gateway directly to the review task.
rules.situation: the description states that one participant reviews an item produced by another participant, and that the same participant then records an outcome on it (such as OK or Not OK) that decides the next step, with the review and the recording of the outcome described as separate actions

rules.instruction: When the description states that a decision or check leads to a named action on the item (for example a stated approval, a required revision, or a detected high-risk condition), and that the action is followed by further steps before the process continues: Model the named action as its own task on the sequence flow of that decision outcome, placed after the gateway and before the next step. Do not connect the decision gateway directly to the following step, and do not fold the action into the gateway label or the next task's label.
rules.situation: the description states a sequence of distinct actions, each performed by a named role (for example examining, writing, then checking an item), where each action follows the previous one, even when the next action is done by a different role

rules.instruction: When the description says one participant produces an output and a different, more senior participant then checks that output, and the check is followed by a separate statement in which the checker records an OK or Not OK decision that routes the flow: Model the check as a task labelled with the checking act and its performer as the description words them. Model the decision as a separate task labelled with the decision act itself (for example the verb of deciding the outcome, with the outcome values), placed after the check and before the exclusive gateway that routes on that outcome. Do not label either task with a generic verb such as record or register, or with the name of a later process step, when the description names a different act. Keep the wording taken from the description.
rules.situation: the description says one participant produces an output and a different, more senior participant then checks that output, and the check is followed by a separate statement in which the checker records an OK or Not OK decision that routes the flow

rules.instruction: When the description states that one outcome of a check sends the flow back to an earlier activity, and that the other outcome says the process proceeds to further handling that is not described as ending it: Do not close the flow with an end event on the outcome that proceeds. Model the continuation the description names as its own task, or as the flow into the next described step, and place the end event only where the description says the process ends. Keep the rework flow on the other outcome as described.
